slides.headline: Mount Everest used to be under the SEA
Its summit was sea floor
slides.body: The rock at the very top is limestone that formed in a warm, shallow sea about 450 million years ago.

slides.headline: There are fossils up there
slides.body: Bits of trilobites, sea lilies and tiny shellfish are in the summit rock. (Trilobite shown: an example, not from Everest.)

slides.headline: India pushed it up
slides.body: The Indian plate slammed into Asia about 55 million years ago and squeezed that old sea floor 5.5 miles into the sky.

slides.headline: 8,848.86 m tall
slides.body: That's the official height Nepal and China announced together in December 2020 (29,032 ft).

slides.headline: It's still rising
slides.body: About 4 inches (10 cm) per century. Your fingernails are faster.
